display.title: Torah Is the Best Merchandise; Me'ayin Yavo Ezri, Part 1
display.summary_short: Learning Torah just for Hashem, shown by a classroom experiment and the story of the Baal Shem Tov's soul, then part 1 of a Chassid's desperate trip to the Rebbe Maharash.
display.summary_long: Just after the Rebbe Rashab's birthday, the storyteller retells how the young Rebbe Rashab cried to his grandfather, the Tzemach Tzedek, because Hashem appeared to Avraham and not to him, and the Rebbe's lesson: we can learn Torah and do mitzvos just for Hashem, without prizes. Speaking as a teacher of young boys, he describes trying this in his class, with a million dollars and a lollipop, children who turned down ice cream, and mothers' notes about quiet good deeds. He then tells of a simple Jew in Tzfas who refused to tell Eliyahu HaNavi what good deed he had done at his bar mitzvah, even in exchange for Torah secrets; a hundred years later that soul came down as the Baal Shem Tov. Story time follows: Reb Shmuel Brin, a devoted Chassid who owns a vodka factory, arrives in Lubavitch weeping. A worker stole from the taxed vat and blamed him, the police locked his factory, and he faces trial and possible exile to Siberia. The Rebbe Maharash gives him instructions, which will be told next week.
display.lesson: Learn Torah and do mitzvos just for Hashem; that connection is the greatest reward. Following a tzaddik's instructions exactly keeps a person safe.
